rationale: No site can be placed from the evidence. The reporter says so, 'I am not getting stack resolved - let me know if this is required to troubleshoot', and the pasted trace is bare addresses, 'mysqld[0xa9b877]', with only the crash handler and plugin_init resolved. What the report does establish is a configuration boundary, since the same build crashes only at page size 32K with a 3M first data file and passes at 16K, 64K, or with a 1M, 11M or 31M first file. That matches the stated rule, that every doublewrite buffer page must fit in the first system data file, so the cause is a capacity limit derived from configuration rather than a fault at any one site.
notes: Twenty-six gold files for one missing capacity check. They are thirteen files mirrored exactly into the InnoDB and XtraDB trees, so the per-file count is doubled by MariaDB shipping two copies of the same storage engine, and the thirteen are themselves one check plus error propagation through every caller that had been ignoring an allocation failure. This is the largest gold set in the sample and the clearest case of file count tracking project structure rather than the size of the defect. The roles rest on the two commit messages, which are unusually explicit about what each function was changed for, rather than on reading eleven hundred diff lines; a rater who worked only from the diff could reasonably label several of the propagation files causal, since each did contain the wrong logic of ignoring a failure return. Worth putting in the agreement check. Note also that this packet lost one file's diff to a renderer cap of 25 files until that cap was raised to 50, and this label was written after the re-render.
